info.name: Bee Flow
info.summary: AI assistant for your Nextcloud — chat with Files, Mail, Calendar, Deck, Notes, Tasks, Contacts and Talk.
info.description:
> **Requires AppAPI with a Docker deploy daemon** (HaRP recommended). Nextcloud All-in-One offers HaRP as an optional container. Bee Flow cannot be installed on managed or shared hosting without Docker. The short [install guide](https://docs.beeflow.ai/getting-started/nextcloud) shows what your Nextcloud needs.
**Bee Flow turns your Nextcloud into an AI workspace.**
Click the bee icon in your top bar and chat with an assistant that already knows your files, mail, calendar and team. Ask it to summarise a long PDF, draft a reply to an email, find that document from last quarter, or schedule a meeting — Bee Flow does the work in the apps you already use.
## What you get
- **You choose where Bee Flow runs.** After installing, an administrator chooses once where Bee Flow runs: **Bee Flow Cloud** — our hosted service, which runs on **Scaleway** with all servers located in **the Netherlands (EU)** — or your own server. Until then nothing leaves your Nextcloud. Sign in with your existing Nextcloud account — no second password, no app-passwords, no API keys to paste anywhere. - **An AI agent with context.** Bee Flow can read and act on **Files, Mail, Calendar, Contacts, Deck, Notes, Tasks, Talk, Activity** and **Notifications** — only on the items you explicitly point it at. - **Built-in privacy shield.** Detects emails, phone numbers, IBANs, BSNs and other sensitive data in your prompts and replaces them with placeholders before anything reaches the language model. The original values are restored in the reply, only on your screen. - **Multi-user from day one.** Mirrors your Nextcloud users and groups automatically. Admins decide which groups get which Bee Flow integrations — disable Talk for interns, enable everything for the leadership team. - **Self-service for organisation admins.** A 4-step onboarding wizard walks the admin through user-sync mode, default permissions and privacy settings the first time they open Bee Flow. Re-configure anytime under Settings → Organisation.
## How it works
This Nextcloud app is a thin connector. It runs as an ExApp container next to your Nextcloud and connects the embedded Bee Flow web client (an open-source React SPA) to the Bee Flow server an administrator chooses: **Bee Flow Cloud**, our hosted service running on **Scaleway** with all servers located in **the Netherlands (EU)**, or your own server. Browser → Nextcloud → connector → Bee Flow server. Your Nextcloud session is the only credential.
**Prefer to keep everything on your own infrastructure?** You can also run Bee Flow fully self-hosted on your own servers — the connector, the SPA and the Bee Flow server are all open source ([Bee-Flow on GitHub](https://github.com/Bee-Flow)), and Bee Flow Cloud runs the very same code. Follow the [self-hosting guide](https://docs.beeflow.ai/self-hosting) to deploy your own Bee Flow server, then choose "Self-hosted" when you open Bee Flow for the first time and enter its address.
## Data flow disclosure
Nothing is sent to any Bee Flow server until an administrator has chosen one. When the administrator connects, the names and e-mail addresses of this Nextcloud's administrators, its address, instance id and version are sent to the chosen server and an organisation is created there. Users and groups are synchronised afterwards.
When you act on a Nextcloud item, the connector sends the item to the chosen Bee Flow server. Specifically:
- **Always** — your Nextcloud user ID, email, display name and group memberships (used to identify your tenant and apply group-based permissions). - **On demand** — the contents of items you explicitly point the assistant at (e.g. an email you ask it to summarise, a file you ask it to read).
Bee Flow **does not** bulk-export file contents, mail bodies, calendars or contacts. The connector forwards individual requests; nothing is copied, mirrored or indexed by default.
When you choose Bee Flow Cloud: it is hosted on **Scaleway**, with all servers located in **the Netherlands (EU)** — your data is processed and stored within the EU. When you choose your own server, it goes there and nowhere else.
Full privacy policy: <https://beeflow.nl/privacy>.
## Getting started
1. Install this app from the Nextcloud App Store. 2. As a Nextcloud administrator, open Bee Flow from the top bar and choose where it runs: Bee Flow Cloud or your own server. 3. The onboarding wizard then runs — pick your user-sync mode and privacy settings. 4. Other users see a "not set up yet" notice, and then a "Setup in progress" screen, until the administrator has finished — then the chat opens for everyone in the chosen sync scope.
## Support
Questions, or want a hand getting set up? Email us at **info@beeflow.nl**. We support Bee Flow Cloud and can also help you get Bee Flow running on a self-managed or self-hosted Nextcloud.

variable.name: BEEFLOW_TENANT_KEY
variable.description: Leave at "auto": a new Bee Flow organisation is created when an administrator connects this Nextcloud, at the server you choose. Override with an existing tenant key only to connect this Nextcloud to an organisation that already exists (e.g. an enterprise reinstall). To join an existing organisation without a key, use a pairing code below.

variable.name: BEEFLOW_API_BASE_URL
variable.description: Leave empty: after installing, an administrator opens Bee Flow and chooses between Bee Flow Cloud and an own server. Nothing is sent anywhere before that choice. Fill this in only to fix the choice at install time: the URL of your own Bee Flow server, or the word cloud for Bee Flow Cloud (hosted by Bee Flow B.V., Netherlands). For Bee Flow Cloud type the word cloud, not its address. A value set here cannot be changed from inside Nextcloud.

variable.name: BEEFLOW_EMBED_BASE_URL
variable.display-name: Bee Flow web app host (optional, advanced)
variable.description: Leave empty in almost all cases. The embedded Bee Flow app then follows the server that is chosen: with Bee Flow Cloud it comes from Cloud's web app, and with a self-hosted server from the web app URL entered next to the server address (on the setup page or under Settings → Artificial Intelligence), or from the copy built into the connector when that is left empty. Set this only to force one web app host whatever server is chosen. Nothing is loaded from it before a server is chosen.

variable.name: BEEFLOW_NC_PUBLIC_URL
variable.description: Address at which the Bee Flow server can call this Nextcloud back when connecting and for user synchronisation. Leave blank if the Bee Flow server can reach your Nextcloud at its main URL — the common case. Set this only if your Nextcloud is behind NAT or only reachable via a tunnel/reverse-proxy. It can also be entered later on the setup page.

variable.name: BEEFLOW_PAIRING_CODE
variable.description: One-shot 8-char code generated by the org admin in an existing Bee Flow organisation (Settings → Organisation → Nextcloud Sync → "Pair a new Nextcloud"). Setting this before first boot binds this Nextcloud to that existing organisation instead of creating a new one. The code is used once, when the connector connects to the server you choose, and ignored afterwards. It can also be entered on the setup page.

variable.name: BEEFLOW_TRUSTED_EMBED_ORIGINS
variable.display-name: Extra origins allowed to embed Bee Flow (optional, advanced)
variable.description: Leave blank in almost all cases. Bee Flow renders inside an iframe on your Nextcloud page and only allows your own Nextcloud origin to frame it. If your users reach Nextcloud through an address the connector never sees — a reverse proxy or a second domain in front of Nextcloud — the embedded app stays blank and the browser console reports a frame-ancestors violation. Add that address here (comma-separated, e.g. https://cloud.example.com). The connector logs the exact origin to add when it blocks one.

variable.name: BEEFLOW_NC_CA_CERT
variable.description: Leave blank in almost all cases. The connector automatically trusts a self-signed or internal-CA Nextcloud certificate on first start (it only does this when the certificate does not already verify, so valid public/Let's Encrypt certificates are unaffected). Set this only if you prefer to pin an explicit trust anchor: paste the PEM certificate (or chain) of your Nextcloud's CA. Has no effect when your Nextcloud already uses a publicly-trusted certificate.

variable.name: BEEFLOW_NC_TLS_PIN
variable.description: "auto" (default) lets the connector trust your Nextcloud's certificate when it is self-signed or signed by an internal CA, so the app can complete setup on local/on-prem installs. The certificate is pinned on first use: the connector remembers its key and refuses a different one, and an administrator accepts a renewed certificate on the connector's setup page. This never weakens a valid public certificate. Set to "off" in security-strict environments to disable automatic trust — then only a publicly-trusted certificate or an explicit "Nextcloud CA certificate" above will be accepted.

variable.name: BEEFLOW_NC_PROXY_MAX_BODY_MB
variable.display-name: Largest upload from Bee Flow to Nextcloud, in MB (optional, advanced)
variable.description: Leave blank in almost all cases (100). The largest body one request from the Bee Flow server into Nextcloud may carry, for example a file an agent writes. 0 means no cap.

variable.name: BEEFLOW_NC_PROXY_MAX_INFLIGHT_MB
variable.display-name: Memory for uploads in progress, in MB (optional, advanced)
variable.description: Leave blank in almost all cases (512). The most upload data all requests from the Bee Flow server together may hold in memory at one moment. 0 means no cap.

variable.name: BEEFLOW_UPSTREAM_HEADERS_TIMEOUT_MS
variable.display-name: Time to wait for the Bee Flow server, in milliseconds (optional, advanced)
variable.description: Leave blank in almost all cases (60000). How long the Bee Flow server may take to start answering a request. 0 switches the timeout off.

variable.name: LOG_LEVEL
variable.description: Leave blank in almost all cases (info). One of: debug, info, warn, error.

variable.name: BEEFLOW_SIG_SKEW_SECONDS
variable.display-name: Allowed clock difference, in seconds (optional, advanced)
variable.description: Leave blank in almost all cases (300). How far the timestamp of a signed request may differ from this host's clock. Accepted range: 30 to 900.

variable.name: BEEFLOW_SERVER_CA_CERT
variable.display-name: Bee Flow server CA certificate (optional, advanced)
variable.description: Leave blank when your Bee Flow server has a certificate from a public certificate authority. For a self-hosted Bee Flow server with a certificate from your own certificate authority, or a self-signed one: the PEM certificate (or chain) to trust, or the path of a PEM file inside the container. It is added to the default certificate authorities and used for the connection to the Bee Flow server only. Certificate verification stays on.

variable.name: HTTPS_PROXY
variable.display-name: Outbound proxy for the Bee Flow server (optional, advanced)
variable.description: Leave blank unless this container reaches the outside only through a forward proxy. The URL of that proxy, for example http://proxy.example.com:3128 (with user:password@ in front of the host when the proxy asks for it). Used for https connections to the Bee Flow server only; Nextcloud is always reached directly.

variable.name: NO_PROXY
variable.display-name: Hosts reached without the outbound proxy (optional, advanced)
variable.description: Only read when an outbound proxy is set above. Comma-separated host names that are reached directly, for example a Bee Flow server inside your own network. Nextcloud does not have to be listed.
